text:
oncall-bot: [PAGER] High NotReady spike in inference-eu-west pool detected. Multiple kubelet restarts observed on gpu nodes; error rates rising for realtime generation routes. Paging rotation: @alex @maria.

alex: I'm on pager. pulling up node list and pod failures.

maria: joining. any customer reports?

jess: CS flagged 2 customers (search-inc, chatly) with ~30s tail latencies and 4-6% 502 failures over last 2 minutes.

alex: kubectl get nodes | grep eu-west-gpu -> 3 nodes NotReady out of 18 in pool. Pod evictions on those nodes, some inference containers restarting.

samir: @alex can you paste the kubelet logs and dmesg for one of the affected nodes? looking for OOM or driver errors.

alex: grabbing logs:
```
-- node: eu-west-gpu-07 --
Mar 10 12:07:11 kubelet[1234]: E030 12:07:11.123 kubelet.go:xxx] kubelet lost heartbeat, restarting
Mar 10 12:07:11 kernel: [ 1234.567890] Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (inference-worker) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 10 12:07:11 nvidia-modeset: NVRM: Xid (79, 0): GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 10 12:07:12 containerd: runtime create: failed to start container: unexpected EOF
```

alex: looks like combined kubelet restarts + GPU driver Xid errors -> container runtime failures and node NotReady.

maria: quick mitigation options:
- cordon+drain affected nodes to stop new pods landing
- bump pool size to absorb traffic (scale up spare nodes)
- enable routing fallback to eu-west-fallback pool or reduce model size for new requests
- taint nodes to drain gracefully if they keep flapping

kevin: I'll open an incident ticket and notify infra. INC-2026-179 created: https://incidents.example/INC-2026-179

samir: I can run a rolling restart of kubelet via systemd on the affected nodes after cordon. also check GPU driver restart script on those hosts.

alex: executing mitigation:
```
kubectl cordon eu-west-gpu-07
kubectl drain eu-west-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl scale deployment inference-worker-eu-west --replicas=22
```

infra-bot: autoscaler: launched 4 new nodes in eu-west (type g4dn.8xlarge), expected join in ~90s.

maria: routing: converting production route 'generation-realtime' to fallback policy (smaller model) to reduce memory footprint while we recover. toggling now.

jess: sending customer comms: short note to search-inc/chatly that we are investigating increased errors and have mitigation in progress.

samir: after cordon/drain I see kubelet service is in CrashLoop on eu-west-gpu-08. journalctl shows:
```
Mar 10 12:08:45 kubelet[1234]: runtime/cgo: pthread_create failed: Resource temporarily unavailable
Mar 10 12:08:45 kubelet[1234]: fatal error: runtime: cannot allocate memory
```

samir: this suggests kernel OOM pressure, maybe noisy tenant or memory leak in inference container. need to evict heavy pods and move traffic.

alex: I patched the eviction priority by adding pod disruption budget tweaks and increased node memory pressure threshold for Kubelet. Also set evictionHard to lower frequency to avoid cold-draining healthy nodes while we stabilize. (will document in incident).

maria: infra team recommends restarting nvidia-driver-daemonset on the affected hosts; I'll trigger a rolling restart of gpu-driver-daemonset with maxUnavailable=1.

kevin: infra oncall @samir-infra is taking lead on driver health. pinged hardware vendor support for Xid codes.

samir: restarted kubelet on eu-west-gpu-07 and eu-west-gpu-08 via systemctl; nodes returned Ready after driver health check passed. eu-west-gpu-09 still NotReady, investigating.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot triggered fallback route: generation-realtime -> generation-fallback at 12:12 UTC.

alex: traffic now at fallback pool; error rates on production generation route dropped from 5% -> 0.8%. latency tail improved but still elevated for some requests hitting cold instances.

jess: Customer update posted: "We are experiencing higher latencies for realtime generation in EU-West due to node instability. We have mitigations in place (traffic fallback, node restart) and expect normal service shortly. Will follow up with root cause." :thumbsup:

maria: action items while stabilizing:
- samir/infra: validate GPU driver logs and collect /var/log/nvidia and dmesg on affected hosts
- alex: collect heap/profile from inference-worker that was OOMing, check for memory leak in model loaders
- kevin: track incident timeline and customer impact metrics, update ticket
- jess: keep CS updates every 30m or on major state change

samir: found heavy memory spike in a specific model shard load path; replicated locally. will rollback a recent model rollout on eu-west to reduce memory footprint.

alex: rolled back model v2.4.1 -> v2.4.0 on eu-west workers, pods started with lower memory use. nodes leaving NotReady -> Ready as eviction pressure eases.

infra-bot: node eu-west-gpu-09 rejoined cluster at 12:20 UTC. all nodes back to Ready (18/18).

oncall-bot: incident status -> Mitigated. routing restored to generation-realtime at 12:23 UTC.

kevin: final numbers: peak 3 nodes NotReady, ~6% error rate at peak, ~2k requests impacted, two paying customers reported visible degradation.

maria: we're keeping the incident open for postmortem. please upload logs and mark any runbook gaps. I'll lead the RCA with infra/rls.

alex: note for postmortem: need better preflight for model rollout memory usage, automatic model health gating, and tighter kubelet OOM monitoring alerts.

jess: letting CS know we will follow-up with postmortem and compensation if needed.

samir: closing run: all mitigation steps documented in INC-2026-179. Will attach driver logs and kubelet journal.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved by oncall rotation. Please ACK and move to postmortem channel if needed. :white_check_mark:
